deals.summary: After 40 years of ownership the Pohlads announced a sale process (Allen & Co. hired, per Sportico); it ended in August 2025 with the family keeping control and adding limited partners.

deals.headline: Twins add three limited partners; Pohlads keep majority
deals.investor: Glick Family Investments; George G. Hicks; Craig Leipold
deals.summary: Glick Family Investments, George G. Hicks and Minnesota Wild owner Craig Leipold bought LP stakes; proceeds pay down debt (Sportico put team debt at about $400m in August 2025). Sportico later stated the LP stakes were sold at a $1.75bn valuation; the stake sold was not disclosed by the club.

name: Minnesota Twins
notes: Founded is the MLB guide's 'Established' year for the Minnesota club (1961); the franchise began as the Washington Senators (Forbes traces it to the 1894 Kansas City Blues). The LP valuation comes from Sportico, March 2026: 'the Twins ended up selling LP stakes last year at a $1.75 billion valuation'. A 20% stake was reported by Sports Illustrated (not citable here); the club declined to state it. Team debt 'approximately $400 million' (Sportico, Aug 2025) is gross debt, so net_debt is left null. The MLB front-office page still lists Jim Pohlad as Control Owner and Chairman of the executive board, while listing Tom Pohlad as Chairman & CEO. Further LPs (Fort Myers Mighty Mussels' managing partners, Feb 2026, per MiLB.com headline) not verified on the page. Forbes figures are 2025-season estimates (Debt/Value 25%). Stadium owner, attendance and social counts not found on a citable page.

ownership_summary: The Pohlad family has owned the Twins since Carl Pohlad bought the club in 1984 for $44m. After exploring a sale from October 2024, the family kept majority control and in December 2025 sold limited-partner stakes to Glick Family Investments, George G. Hicks and Craig Leipold (Sportico: at a $1.75bn valuation), using proceeds to pay down debt; Tom Pohlad became chairman and CEO and control person (pending MLB approval).
